rv.q: This is nonetheless a generous, affirmative show that enjoyed a warm and supportive reaction from its audience.
LAST NIGHT AND THE NIGHT BEFORE is a moving portrait of a Black family navigating a pivotal moment of transition.
In Grays’ final, devastating twist, we see two parents so devoted they’ll use any means necessary to protect a child who would do the same to protect them.
You will be emotionally drained but glad you witnessed this flawless production by the exceptional playwright Donnetta Lavinia Grays.
The play unfolds with surprising tragic revelations and resolves in heart-wrenching and hopeful ways.
Valerie Curtis-Newton’s sharp direction creates a through line, so the incidents and relationships are reinforcing rather than muddling.
The play, which is filled with mystery and amour, will touch audiences with its tenderness.
The play that follows portrays complicated but loving relationships, with many time shifts from past to present.
In my opinion, Donnetta Lavinia Grays’ “Last Night….” suffers from a lack of a clear antagonist.
